S67.01.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder
steps: Open a terminal in a project folder and run: agi
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Explain the structure of this repository: main parts, entry points and how they fit together
Press Enter and wait for the answer
Check that the answer names the main folders, the entry points and how they connect, in plain words
S67.01.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.02.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder
S67.02.note: The search tools are defined in apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs; the plan's line numbers moved.
steps: Run: agi in a project folder
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Where is the main chat loop implemented? Give file and line.
Press Enter and wait
Check that the answer gives a file path and line number and the code there matches
S67.02.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.03.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder
steps: Run: agi in a project folder
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Where is the function named run_review used across the repository?
Press Enter and wait
Check that the answer lists each use with file and line, and that they match a search of the folder
S67.03.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.04.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder
S67.04.note: The search tools are defined in apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs; the plan's line numbers moved.
steps: Run: agi in a project folder
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Trace how the /review command flows from the input box to the review prompt, step by step, with file and line
Press Enter and wait
Check that the steps follow the code in order, from the command handler to the prompt it sends
S67.04.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.05.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder
steps: Run: agi in a project folder
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type a free question about the project, for example: How are project instructions files like AGENTS.md loaded?
Press Enter and wait
Check that the answer is based on the files and matches what the files say
S67.05.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.06.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a copy of a git project to change
S67.06.note: The approval title for file edits was not found in production code; only the choice labels are cited.
steps: Run: agi in a copy of a git project (not your real work)
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type a small feature request, for example: Add a function that returns the project name, in a new file
Press Enter; when an approval box appears, read it and press Enter on "Yes" or choose "No"
After the turn, look for the line "Files changed this turn" and check that the new or edited file exists in the folder
S67.06.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.07.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a copy of a git project that has a known defect
S67.07.note: The approval title for file edits was not found in production code; only the choice labels are cited.
steps: Run: agi in a copy of a git project (not your real work)
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type a defect to fix, for example: The total is off by one in the sum function; find the cause and fix it
Press Enter; on each approval box press "Yes" or choose "No"
Check the answer names the cause and the line changed, and the "Files changed this turn" line lists the file
S67.07.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.08.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a copy of a git project to change
steps: Run: agi in a copy of a git project (not your real work)
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Move the helper functions in this file into a new module, without changing behaviour
Press Enter; on each approval box press "Yes" or choose "No"
Check the new module exists, the old file calls it, and the tests still pass when you run them yourself
S67.08.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.09.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a copy of a git project with an existing test file
steps: Run: agi in a copy of a git project (not your real work)
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Write new unit tests for the sum function in the existing test file
Press Enter; on each approval box press "Yes" or choose "No"
Check that the new test cases appear in the file and that they match the function's behaviour
S67.09.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.10.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder with a test suite
S67.10.note: The agent chooses the test command; there is no dedicated control.
steps: Run: agi in a project folder that has a test suite
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Run the project's test suite and tell me the result
Press Enter; if an approval box appears for the command, press "Yes"
Check that the answer reports the command it ran and the pass or fail counts, and that they match the terminal output
S67.10.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.11.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a copy of a project with a failing test
S67.11.note: The agent chooses the test command; there is no dedicated control.
steps: Run: agi in a project folder whose tests fail (a copy made for testing)
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Run the tests, then explain why the first failing test fails
Press Enter; press "Yes" on any command approval box
Check that the answer quotes the failure message and names the file and line it points to
S67.11.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.12.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder with a type checker
S67.12.note: The agent chooses the checker command; there is no dedicated control.
steps: Run: agi in a project folder that uses a type checker
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Run the type checker and report the errors
Press Enter; press "Yes" on any command approval box
Check that the answer lists the errors with file and line, and that they match the checker output in the terminal
S67.12.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.13.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder with a linter
S67.13.note: The agent chooses the lint command; there is no dedicated control.
steps: Run: agi in a project folder that has a linter
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Run the linter and report the findings
Press Enter; press "Yes" on any command approval box
Check that the answer lists the findings and that they match the linter output in the terminal
S67.13.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.14.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder with a build step
S67.14.note: The agent chooses the build command; there is no dedicated control.
steps: Run: agi in a project folder that has a build step
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Build the application and report whether it succeeded
Press Enter; press "Yes" on any command approval box
Check that the answer says success or failure and that it matches the build output in the terminal
S67.14.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

labels.text: List subagent tasks and background commands

S67.15.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder with a development server
S67.15.note: Background start is set by the agent's command option run_in_background (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/bash/mod.rs).
steps: Run: agi in a project folder that has a development server
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Start the development server and keep it running while you work on something else
Press Enter and wait for the answer; then type: /tasks and press Enter
Check that the server is listed as a background command with an id, and that the app it serves responds in a browser
S67.15.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"; then /tasks

S67.16.needs: A paired AGI Desktop with the AGI Chrome extension
S67.16.note: Browser tools include browser_navigate, browser_read_page and browser_screenshot (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs).
steps: Open AGI Desktop, install the AGI Chrome extension and pair it, as the Chrome status message asks
Run: agi, then type: /chrome and press Enter
Read the "Chrome integration" block; it should say the browser is paired
Type at the box "Message AGI...  / for commands": Open the page in the paired browser, read its main heading, and take a screenshot
Check that the answer shows the heading and a screenshot is taken, and that the page matches the browser

S67.20.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a git project with uncommitted changes
S67.20.note: /review accepts an optional effort word and scope, for example /review low src/auth.
steps: In a git project, change one file without committing
Run: agi, then type: /review and press Enter
Wait for the answer; read the overall verdict and each issue
Check that each issue names a file and line, and that the lines match the uncommitted change

labels.text: Review a hosted pull request by number, URL or branch, read with the GitHub CLI.
Post the review to the pull request as a comment.

S67.21.needs: GitHub CLI signed in with access to a test pull request; --post writes a real comment, so use a test pull request only
S67.21.note: The in-chat /review command does not take a pull request; this is the terminal command.
steps: In a project folder with the GitHub CLI signed in, run: agi review --pr <number of a test pull request>
Wait for the review; read the findings it prints
Check that the findings match the pull request's diff on GitHub
Only for a test pull request, add --post to post the review as a comment and check the comment appears on the pull request

S67.22.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project folder
steps: Run: agi, then type: /security-review and press Enter
In the "Security review scope" box choose "Changed files only" or "Whole repository" and press Enter
Wait for the answer
Check that it lists security findings with file and line, and that they match the code

S67.23.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a project with a known issue
S67.23.note: The findings are written in the chat, so the explanation depends on the model's answer.
steps: Run /review or /security-review in a project with a known issue
Wait for the answer
Read each finding; it should give the file, the line and a plain-language explanation
Check that each explanation matches the code at that location

S67.24.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a throwaway copy of a git project (the discard key is destructive)
S67.24.note: /diff-review is not listed in the / palette or help, but the typed command is handled (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs). Its own text names it a per-file review, not a patch proposal.
steps: Run: agi in a throwaway copy of a git project
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" ask for a change to a file
When an approval box appears, read the file name and the lines shown before choosing "Yes" or "No"
After the change, type: /diff-review and press Enter
In the "Diff Review" box, read the file and its diff before pressing y or n
S67.24.where: agi, then /diff-review (review the agent's changed files before they are kept)

labels.text: y approve   n reject   s skip   ↑↓ navigate   Enter done

S67.25.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a throwaway copy of a git project (d twice discards an unstaged hunk and cannot be undone)
S67.25.note: Differs from Expected: y approves a whole file and Enter stages approved files with git add, so the user picks files or hunks of the working tree, not the agent's proposed patches. /diff-review is not in the / palette.
steps: In a throwaway copy of a git project, make changes to two files
Run: agi, then type: /diff-review and press Enter
In the "Diff Review" box press y on the file to keep, n to reject, s to skip; move with the arrow keys
Press Enter to finish, then run git status in the folder
Check that only the files you pressed y on are staged

S67.26.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a copy of a project folder to change
S67.26.note: /init only creates AGENTS.md; other documentation is a typed request.
steps: Run: agi in a copy of a project folder
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Update the README with a short section that explains the main commands, from the code
Press Enter; press "Yes" on any file approval box
Check that the README changed and that each new statement matches the code
S67.26.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"; /init makes AGENTS.md

S67.27.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a copy of a project with migrations (do not run against a real database)
S67.27.note: The agent chooses the migration commands; there is no dedicated control.
steps: Run: agi in a copy of a project that has a schema or migration step
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Add a migration that adds a new column, following the existing migration pattern
Press Enter; press "Yes" on each approval box
Check that a new migration file exists and the existing migrations were not changed
S67.27.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.28.needs: An AGI CLI signed in; a copy of a project with a dependency to upgrade
S67.28.note: The agent chooses the package commands; there is no dedicated control.
steps: Run: agi in a copy of a project with an out-of-date dependency
At the box "Message AGI...  / for commands" type: Upgrade the dependency named X to its latest version and adjust the code that breaks
Press Enter; press "Yes" on each approval box
Check that the manifest version changed, the lock file was updated by the package manager, and the code still builds when you run it yourself
S67.28.where: agi, then type in the box "Message AGI...  / for commands"

S67.29.needs: a git repository with a staged change, and a signed-in account that can run the agent
S67.29.note: The commit is made only by the agent's git_commit tool; no slash command or CLI subcommand creates a commit directly. Hook prompts are shown as the code describes but were not exercised.
steps: Start agi in a git repository and stage a small change, for example with git add outside agi.
Type a request such as: commit the staged changes with the message "docs: fix typo".
When the approval line appears, read it. It should begin with "Commit:" and show the message subject.
Approve it, then run git log -1 in another terminal and compare the commit message with what was approved and with Expected.
S67.29.where: agi, then ask the agent in the chat to commit the staged changes (there is no /commit command; the agent runs its git_commit tool)

S67.30.needs: a git repository, and a signed-in account that can run the agent
S67.30.note: /fork and /branch in the chat are conversation branches, not git branches. The agent's branch tool creates the branch without switching to it, so a switch needs a separate request.
steps: Start agi in a git repository.
Type a request such as: create a branch named feature/test-branch from HEAD.
When the approval line appears, check it mentions "branch create".
Approve it, then run git branch in another terminal and compare with Expected. Note that git_branch_create does not switch to the new branch.
S67.30.where: agi, then ask the agent in the chat to create a branch (there is no branch slash command; the agent runs its git_branch_create tool)

S67.32.needs: GitHub CLI signed in, a pull request with review comments, and its branch checked out
S67.32.note: The fix-mode refusal text is in apps/cli/src/pr_feedback.rs; the fix itself was not verified by reading the code.
steps: On a checkout of a pull request branch with review comments, start agi in that folder.
Type /pr-comments 123 (use your pull request number) and read the feedback the agent shows.
Type /autofix-pr 123 and add an instruction such as: address the review comments.
Check that the agent edits files, and compare the result with Expected. If the checkout is on another branch, the message asks you to run gh pr checkout first.
S67.32.where: agi, then type /pr-comments <number> to read review comments, or /autofix-pr <number> to have the agent change the code

labels.text: Plan a goal into steps and run them as subagents

S67.36.needs: a signed-in account and a project folder
S67.36.note: No single goal-and-bound command was found; the bound is set by --max-turns, --effort, or /budget and the loop by /workflow. The stop-at-bound message was not located in the code.
steps: Start agi with agi --max-turns 5 in a project folder.
Type /workflow followed by a goal, such as: add a short README section about setup.
Watch the stages and subagent steps the agent shows.
Check that the run ends when the goal is done or stops at the turn limit, and compare with Expected. For a spend bound, type /budget 50 first and see the confirmation text.
S67.36.where: agi --max-turns 5, then type /workflow <goal> in the chat; the turn bound also comes from agi --effort low|medium|high|max and /budget <credits>

S67.37.needs: a project folder (a project root is required for the project tier)
S67.37.note: Only the save path was read; the reuse in later sessions depends on the memory loading code, which was not traced end to end.
steps: In a project folder, type /memory add project Use tabs for indentation.
Read the confirmation text, which starts with "Appended to" and shows the file path.
Quit agi, start it again in the same folder, and ask: what indentation style should you use?
Check that the answer uses the saved fact, and compare with Expected.
S67.37.where: Type /memory add project <text> in the chat, then start agi again in the same folder and ask about it

S67.38.needs: a test folder you create yourself, outside the project folder, and a signed-in account
S67.38.note: Instruction files are loaded by compaction::load_instructions and the app_server surfaces code; no screen lists the loaded files was found.
steps: In an empty test folder outside the project, create a file named AGENTS.md that says: always end every reply with the word DONE.
Start agi in that folder and ask a simple question.
Check that the reply ends with DONE, and compare with Expected.
S67.38.where: no control; the effect shows in the agent's replies in a folder that contains AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md

S67.39.needs: a test folder you create, and a signed-in account
S67.39.note: The skills list hides disabled skills by the code in apps/cli/src/skills.rs; the on-screen result was not run.
steps: Create a skill file ending in .md in .agiworkforce/skills/ in a test folder, then start agi there.
Type /skills and find the skill name in the list headed Skills (N).
Type /skills-toggle, move to the skill with the arrow keys, press Space to turn it off, then Enter to save.
Type /skills again and check that it is gone from the list, then type /plugin and compare with Expected.
S67.39.where: agi, then type /skills to list skills, /skills-toggle to turn them on or off, and /plugin to see plugins
